text:
alex: Heads-up — scheduling a controlled rollout for llmroute_v4 in 10m. Plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over ~40m with health gates. Rollback triggers: error rate +2% absolute, p95 latency +150ms, or request errors in telemetry. Release notes: https://go.redwood/release/1234 :thread-announce:

maria: thanks. tagging @sahil for oncall coverage. which cohorts are we touching?

sahil: oncall here, I can watch. please post the exact thresholds and the commands you’ll run so I can intervene quickly.

alex: thresholds below and commands to run live:
```
# start canary to 5% on canary cohort
ffctl set llmroute_v4 --cohort=canary --pct=5 --by=version
# pin default traffic back to v3.9 if rollback
ffctl pin llmroute --version=v3.9 --cohort=default
```
Ramp cadence: 5% (10m) -> 25% (20m) -> 100% (40m) if green. Quiet window: 0200-0500 UTC avoided.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for llmroute_v4 — 5% to cohort=canary (started at 6498761111) :rocket:

lucy: Observability check: p50/p95/p99 currently 22ms / 51ms / 120ms on canary, error rate 0.03% — looks normal so far.

maria: OK. if metrics hold for 10m, we’ll shift to 25%. @sahil will you escalate on any latency >150ms p95 or error jumps?

sahil: yes. I’ll escalate on slack + pager if thresholds hit. Also please ensure model warmup TTL is 15m — some latency spikes stem from cold starts.

alex: warmup TTL confirmed 15m. moving to lift to 25% in 10m unless we see signal.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Scheduled ramp to 25% in 9m — will post update when shift occurs.

oncall-bot: ALERT (us-west-2): p95 latency spike detected: 230ms on llmroute (canary cohort) — 1m ago.

lucy: I’m seeing the same on dashboard, small spike concentrated on requests with long context.

maria: hmm — not widespread errors, but latency > threshold. hold the ramp.

sahil: pausing ramp now. hold at 5%. Beginning triage — if spike persists for 5m, roll back canary.

alex: agreed. execute quick rollback to limit blast: run pin to v3.9 for default and remove v4 from canary.
```
# immediate rollback commands
ffctl set llmroute_v4 --cohort=canary --pct=0
ffctl pin llmroute --version=v3.9 --cohort=default --reason="canary_latency_spike"
```

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Rollback executed — llmroute_v4 removed from canary, default traffic pinned to v3.9. Actions logged. (6498761215) :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: https://go.redwood/incident/987 — latency spike during canary, auto-rollback triggered.

sahil: Postmortem doc created, I’ll own follow-up. Initial hypothesis: warmup isn't covering the long-context traffic pattern; infra team to validate kernel selection for long sequences.

maria: I’ll re-run perf harness against long-context samples and try a warmup batch job to pre-populate KV caches.

lucy: Observability: metrics returned to baseline ~30s after rollback. p95 back to 48ms, error rate 0.02%.

alex: thanks everyone. we’ll re-schedule the rollout after fixes and add an extra warmup step to canary. Closing this ops thread — will link PR + changelog when ready.

maria: noted — will update release notes with canary findings and next steps. +1 on extra warmup and narrower initial cohort next time.

sahil: closing monitoring loop, will watch for any regressions over next hour.

alex: thread closed.
